import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy.signal import find_peaks, savgol_filter
from scipy.ndimage import median_filter
df=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv')
x=df.shift_cm1.values; y=df.intensity.values
# spike check: point deviating strongly from median of neighbours
med=median_filter(y,size=5)
d=y-med
idx=np.argsort(d)[::-1][:10]
for i in idx: print('spike cand',x[i],y[i],round(d[i],1))
# baseline: rolling minimum-based
from scipy.ndimage import minimum_filter1d, uniform_filter1d
base=uniform_filter1d(minimum_filter1d(y,101),101)
ys=savgol_filter(y,7,3)
r=ys-base
pk,pr=find_peaks(ys,prominence=150,width=2)
for p in pk: print(round(x[p],1), round(ys[p],0), 'prom',round(pr['prominences'][list(pk).index(p)],0))
print('baseline range',base.min(),base.max())
"

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from lmfit import Model
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel, VoigtModel, LinearModel, PolynomialModel
df=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv')
x=df.shift_cm1.values; y=df.intensity.values
# global model: 4 peaks (Voigt) + polynomial baseline over full range
def fit(lo,hi,centers,deg=2):
    m=(x>=lo)&(x<=hi)
    xx=x[m]; yy=y[m]
    mod=PolynomialModel(degree=deg,prefix='b_')
    pars=mod.make_params(c0=4500,c1=0,c2=0)
    for i,c in enumerate(centers):
        pk=LorentzianModel(prefix=f'p{i}_')
        pars.update(pk.make_params(center=c,amplitude=2000,sigma=3))
        mod=mod+pk
    r=mod.fit(yy,pars,x=xx)
    return r,xx,yy
r,xx,yy=fit(90,270,[104.7,205.2,243.8])
print(r.fit_report(min_correl=0.9))
" 2>&1 | head -120

print('chi2red',r.redchi)

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel, PolynomialModel
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
df=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv')
x=df.shift_cm1.values; y=df.intensity.values
m=(x>=505)&(x<=537)
mod=PolynomialModel(degree=1,prefix='b_')+LorentzianModel(prefix='s_')
pars=mod.make_params(b_c0=5000,b_c1=0)
pars.update(LorentzianModel(prefix='s_').make_params(center=520.7,amplitude=30000,sigma=2))
r=mod.fit(y[m],pars,x=x[m])
print('Si Lor: center',round(r.params['s_center'].value,2),'+/-',round(r.params['s_center'].stderr,3),'FWHM',round(2*r.params['s_sigma'].value,2),'redchi',round(r.redchi))
print('residual sd in Si window', np.std(r.residual))
# full-range 4-peak fit with broad baseline (poly deg 3) and residual scan
mod=PolynomialModel(degree=3,prefix='b_')
pars=mod.make_params(b_c0=4500,b_c1=0,b_c2=0,b_c3=0)
for i,c in enumerate([104.6,205.4,243.9,520.6]):
    pk=LorentzianModel(prefix=f'p{i}_')
    pars.update(pk.make_params(center=c,amplitude=20000,sigma=3))
    mod=mod+pk
r=mod.fit(y,pars,x=x)
print('overall redchi',round(r.redchi),'resid sd',round(np.std(r.residual),1))
res=r.residual
from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter1d
rs=uniform_filter1d(res,5)
pk,_=find_peaks(rs,height=2.5*np.std(rs))
for p in pk: print('residual bump at',x[p],'smoothed resid',round(rs[p],0))
for i in range(4): print('p',i,'center',round(r.params[f'p{i}_center'].value,2),'fwhm',round(2*r.params[f'p{i}_sigma'].value,2),'amp',round(r.params[f'p{i}_amplitude'].value,0))
"

candidates.evidence: Layered selenide with a strong low-frequency mode near 105 cm-1 and several modes between about 150 and 250 cm-1 with no mode above ~250 cm-1, which is qualitatively like the measured pattern. The 205 and 244 cm-1 assignments are recalled from memory, not checked against a reference spectrum.

Layered group-IV monochalcogenide whose Raman modes lie in the 100-260 cm-1 range, consistent with the absence of peaks above ~250 cm-1 here. Recalled literature positions differ from the measured 105/205/244 cm-1 by more than 10 cm-1, so this is a weak match.
Same Pnma layered family as GeS and SnSe, with modes in the 100-250 cm-1 window. No reliable reference positions were available to compare against, so this rests on structural class only.

Layered pentagonal diselenide with several Raman modes between about 130 and 260 cm-1. Recalled positions are approximate and unverified; the pattern here (one weak low-frequency mode and two strong modes near 205 and 244 cm-1) is not confirmed by any reference.

candidates.evidence: Layered selenide with a strong low-frequency mode near 105 cm-1 and several modes between about 150 and 250 cm-1 with no mode above ~250 cm-1, which is qualitatively like the measured pattern. The 205 and 244 cm-1 assignments are recalled from memory, not checked against a reference spectrum.

Layered group-IV monochalcogenide whose Raman modes lie in the 100-260 cm-1 range, consistent with the absence of peaks above ~250 cm-1 here. Recalled literature positions differ from the measured 105/205/244 cm-1 by more than 10 cm-1, so this is a weak match.
Same Pnma layered family as GeS and SnSe, with modes in the 100-250 cm-1 window. No reliable reference positions were available to compare against, so this rests on structural class only.

Layered pentagonal diselenide with several Raman modes between about 130 and 260 cm-1. Recalled positions are approximate and unverified; the pattern here (one weak low-frequency mode and two strong modes near 205 and 244 cm-1) is not confirmed by any reference.
